title: Cloudy with a Chance of Dust
caption: The star-forming nebula RCW 36, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: RCW 36 · constellation Vela · about 2300 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Clouds strewn across this picture are thick enough in places to block the light behind them, leaving patches and wisps of inky black. This is RCW 36, also called Gum 20, an emission nebula in the constellation Vela, the Sails. At about 2,300 light-years away, it is among the nearest places to our Solar System where massive stars are forming.

Those dark clouds may look lifeless, but they are exactly where stars form. Inside them, clumps of dust and molecular hydrogen fall inward and pull together into new stars, which can end up with small families of planets around them, like our own Solar System.

RCW 36 is only one part of a larger star-forming complex known as the Vela Molecular Ridge. The picture was taken with FORS, an instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope that combines a camera with a spectrograph.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.18 x 7.17 arcminutes) and distance (2300 light years), the frame spans roughly 4.8 × 4.8 light-years. Its light set out about 2,300 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The VLT's FORS2 instrument took this visible-light image through broadband filters and filters for oxygen and hydrogen-alpha emission. The color mapping isn't published.

explore: This image was produced by ESO's Cosmic Gems program, which uses telescope time that cannot be used for science to make outreach images of interesting objects. The data are also placed in ESO's science archive, where astronomers can use them.
alt: Glowing clouds with patches and wisps of inky black dust.
